clue.text: Atmosphere created by song's tempo

blocks.note: an air is a song or tune, with the possessive 's kept
tempo is the speed or pace of something

explanation.surface: A musician says the mood in the room comes from how fast the song is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the portion of the atmosphere above a country, so atmosphere stands in for it loosely.

clue.text: Function of cost divided by time

indicators.note: a word divided by another has that other word sitting in the gap in its middle

blocks.note: a fee is a charge or cost
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Sounds like a maths exercise: a function defined as cost divided by time.
explanation.walkthrough: The mathematical vocabulary is a disguise: function means a social event, and divided by means split open to take a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor social occasion, and function is a common term for any organised event or party.

clue.text: Person receiving charge for cycling?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone being accused or billed, as in a criminal charge or a fee
setter's reading: electrical charge put into a battery so a bicycle can be ridden with motor help

explanation.walkthrough: Charge looks like an accusation or a bill, perhaps for a cycling offence; it is the electricity in the battery of a powered bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider of an electric bicycle charges its battery in order to go cycling, which the question mark flags as a whimsical description.

clue.text: Reduce competition between supermodels?

blocks.note: first meaning: to fade or lessen gradually, as an effect does
second meaning: a whimsical contest, like a play-off or face-off, in which models compete at wearing clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is an invented word in the pattern of play-off and bake-off, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: When an effect wears off it diminishes over time, so the phrasal verb works as a synonym for lessening.

clue.text: Ingredients made from drug-injected pedigree offspring

indicators.note: something injected is put inside a body, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: stock means lineage or breeding
cubs are the young of animals like lions and bears
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A grim kitchen tale of ingredients obtained from doped young pedigree animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock cubes are compressed blocks of dried broth, used as an ingredient to flavour soups and stews.

clue.text: Ships final 75 per cent of young chickens

indicators.note: keeping only the last three quarters means the front quarter of the word is cut away

blocks.note: broilers are young chickens raised for roasting or grilling

explanation.surface: A poultry farmer sends most of the young birds off by ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The eight-letter source loses its first two letters, a quarter of its length.
explanation.definitionFit: Oilers are tankers, vessels built to carry oil, so they are a kind of ship.

clue.text: Disarming soldiers, army originally enters Oxford college

indicators.note: originally points to the start, so only the opening letter of the word is wanted
a piece that enters something goes inside it

blocks.note: LI stands for Light Infantry
Keble is a college of Oxford University
the opening letter of army

explanation.surface: Soldiers lay down their weapons while an army moves into an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: Disarming looks military beside soldiers and army, but it is the definition, meaning charming.
explanation.definitionFit: A disarming person wins people over by being pleasant, which is close to being easy to like.

clue.text: Item a group set apart

blocks.note: first meaning: a single particular or feature
second meaning: a small body of soldiers or staff assigned to a special duty

explanation.walkthrough: The military sense is the less familiar one: a detail is a squad told off for a particular task.
explanation.definitionFit: A detail is an individual point in a list, and in military use a small party separated off for a job.

clue.text: Padre is about to throw in the towel

indicators.note: about suggests turning round and moving the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chaplain is on the point of giving up altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: About is not 'on the point of' but the signal to rearrange the seven letters before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, and throwing in the towel is the boxing idiom for giving up.

clue.text: Yell, perhaps, of some returning gospel singers

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is needed
returning means going back, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of gospel and the start of singers

explanation.surface: Someone describes the shouting of gospel singers as they come back on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Yell is not a shout but an island in Shetland, off the north of Scotland; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Yell is one of the Shetland Islands, so it is an example of an island, a definition by example.

clue.text: Communist leaders in Korea heard voices describing attack by revolutionary

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters, so only each opening letter is kept
to describe can mean to draw a line around, so these letters surround the rest

blocks.note: the opening letters of these three words
to rush is to charge at or attack
Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: Reads like a news report of communist leaders in Korea hearing of an attack by a revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The three initials split around the middle pieces, two before and one after. Leaders sounds like the definition but is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikita Khrushchev led the Soviet Union in the 1950s and 60s, so he was a prominent communist.

clue.text: Sign of modern culture finally changing direction

indicators.note: the last letter is swapped from one compass or hand direction to its opposite

blocks.note: cancel culture is a modern phenomenon of shunning people online
R for right replaces L for left

explanation.surface: A cultural commentator spots a sign that modern culture is at last changing course.
explanation.walkthrough: Modern culture is a cue for the word that comes before culture in the modern phrase cancel culture; its final L (left) becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the crab, so sign is a broad category for it.

clue.text: Permanent way to reduce one's laundry load?

definitions.text: way to reduce one's laundry load

blocks.note: first meaning: never altering, constant

blocks.clueFragment: way to reduce one's laundry load
blocks.note: second meaning: read as two words, a playful instruction to swap clothes less often

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into a verb and an adverb: put on fresh clothes less often and there is less washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchanging stays the same for ever, so it is permanent; the jokey split gives advice for less washing.

clue.text: Swiss ready to welcome current saint

indicators.note: to welcome a guest is to take them inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: ready is slang for cash, and the Swiss currency is the franc
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: The Swiss are prepared to receive a living saint, perhaps on a papal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready looks like an adjective, but it is British slang for money, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: St Francis of Assisi is one of the best-known saints, so the name is an example of a saint.

clue.text: Denied new trading estate lacks versatile traits

indicators.note: something that lacks certain parts is missing them, so these letters are taken away
versatile means adaptable, so the letters to be taken away may come from any position in any order
new suggests remaking what remains in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these six letters are removed

explanation.surface: A refusal: a newly built industrial estate is said to lack adaptable qualities.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike T, R, A, I, T, S from the thirteen letters of trading estate and seven remain, D, N, G, E, A, T, E, which are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or contradict it, so negated and denied are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Slips away after date comes back carrying drinks

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards
something carrying a load holds it inside

blocks.note: to see someone is to date them
an animal laps, or drinks with its tongue

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off after their date returns holding drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: After is a link here; the wordplay alone builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes by, and slipping away is an idiomatic way to describe time passing.

clue.text: Legal document for motel owner not complete

indicators.note: a word that is not complete has lost something, here its final letter

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
Norman Bates runs the motel in Hitchcock's Psycho

explanation.surface: A legal paper is drawn up on behalf of a motel proprietor, but left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: For looks like a link word but supplies three letters; the motel owner is from the film Psycho.
explanation.definitionFit: Probate is the official certificate that a will is valid, issued by a court, so it is a legal document.

clue.text: Farewell to many nude loves

indicators.note: a nude figure has its outer covering removed, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
oodles means lots, and its outer letters are stripped
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O; two of them

explanation.surface: Someone bids goodbye to a crowd of naked lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: Many must first become the slang word oodles, which then loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-oo is a jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye, so it is a farewell.

clue.text: Treatment that requires us to stand up in small space

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means rising from bottom to top, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hiatus is a gap or break; its last two letters are the us of the clue

explanation.surface: A therapy that makes us stand up in a cramped room.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for space already ends in US; that ending is turned upside down in place, after an S for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiatsu is a Japanese massage therapy using finger pressure, so it is a kind of treatment.

clue.text: Hack drinking round – good whiskey and moonshine

indicators.note: something drinking takes liquid inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: to hash is to chop or hack up
O is round in shape
G is the abbreviation for good
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A journalist knocks back a round of good whiskey and some illicit spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey and moonshine both look like drink; moonshine is the definition in its sense of foolish talk, and whiskey is a NATO alphabet letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonshine can mean silly, fanciful nonsense, which is what hogwash means.

clue.text: Loudly criticise letters from the clergy defending king

indicators.note: defenders surround what they protect, so these letters go around another

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of the and the start of clergy
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Clergy are shouted at for defending the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters from signals taking a consecutive run out of the clergy, which then opens to take the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To heckle is to interrupt a speaker with jeers, a noisy form of criticism.

clue.text: Cleric recalled corrupt fool

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
a sap is a gullible fool

explanation.surface: A priest has been withdrawn for being a corrupt idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a minister in charge of a congregation, so is a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Tense knight goes for control

indicators.note: something that goes leaves, so it is removed from the word

blocks.note: the present is a grammatical tense
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A nervous knight goes in search of control.
explanation.walkthrough: Tense looks like an adjective for nervous, but it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A preset is a control or setting fixed in advance, such as a stored station button on a radio.

clue.text: Food book cover

blocks.note: Eccles is the short form of Ecclesiastes, a book of the Bible
to cake something is to coat or cover it thickly

explanation.surface: A cookbook jacket, or food used to cover a book.
explanation.walkthrough: Book cover reads as a single noun, but splits into two pieces. An Eccles cake is a British currant-filled pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a small round flaky pastry filled with currants, so it is an item of food.

clue.text: Upper-class women occasionally featured in Greek plays

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only letters at intervals are kept

blocks.note: every third letter, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Posh ladies sometimes take parts in Greek dramas.
explanation.walkthrough: Gels is a jokey spelling of girls as said in a cut-glass British accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Gels mimics the upper-class pronunciation of girls, so the word itself denotes well-bred young women.

clue.text: University members try to suppress opponents

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
West and North are opposing players at bridge

explanation.surface: Students attempt to crush their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, suppress means sit on top of, so GO comes above the bridge pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Gown stands for the academic members of a university town, from the gowns they wear, as in town and gown.

clue.text: Benefits of programming language applications

blocks.note: PL, as in PL/I, a programming language
applications are uses to which something is put

explanation.surface: A software engineer weighs up the advantages of coding apps.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluses are advantages or positive points, so they are benefits.

clue.text: Author Christopher heading off for Robin's home

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: Christopher Isherwood, author of Goodbye to Berlin

explanation.surface: A writer sets off for Robin's house.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin is not a bird but Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is the legendary hideout of the outlaw Robin Hood.
